gaps.sentence: The candidate ___ speech impressed us most got the job.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose speech' — the speech belonged to the candidate.

gaps.sentence: There are times ___ I really miss my home town.
gaps.explanation: 'There are times when ...' is a standard pattern; 'when' stands for 'at which'.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: The film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: After a comma, 'that' is impossible: use 'which'.

gaps.sentence: I will always remember the summer ___ we cycled along the Danube.
gaps.explanation: 'When' relates to a time expression like 'the summer'.

gaps.sentence: Do you remember the time ___ we got lost in Rome?
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces defining clauses after 'the time'; 'which' would need a preposition.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: The police have arrested the man ___ stole the painting.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people in defining clauses.
